endorsements.quote: Given this limited transparency and the variability introduced by different EHR environments, health care provider organizations may benefit from conducting local usability evaluations.
In-situ pilot testing in live clinical environments is critical as system-level behaviors cannot be meaningfully inferred from simulations, vendor demonstrations, or usability sessions alone.
Version tracking and deliberate postdeployment evaluation are essential to evaluate the phenomenon of model drift rather than relying solely on initial preimplementation testing.
Quantitative data may include changes in documentation time, note completeness, coding patterns, message turnaround times, or visit length.

Assessing the costs and benefits, including total cost of ownership, needs to be a key part of core implementation metrics to ensure that financial viability is taken into account before final procurement decisions are made.
At the system level, the organization pilots both tools in a small number of clinical settings with different workflows and documentation norms.

Because models evolve rapidly through updates to prompts, parameters, and foundational components, version tracking and reproducible testing protocols are essential for health care provider organizations to maintain an accurate understanding of model behavior.

unlisted_practices: Health care provider organizations should implement continuous monitoring as vendors update prompts, parameters, or foundational models and as clinician behavior evolves.
Health care provider organizations and vendors should collaborate on implementation science to improve outcomes.
Health care provider organizations should evaluate ASR performance across accents, dialects, multilingual speech, background noise, and multispeaker encounters.

screen.reason: This is a framework/perspective paper presenting a conceptual model and recommendations for health systems evaluating and adopting ambient AI technologies.
